info.name: Community Waste Collection API
info.description: Household and pickup lifecycle checkpoint. Start Docker Compose and run requests in order. Households cleans up its own unreferenced record. Pickups creates a dedicated household per run and retains canceled pickup history; existing records are preserved. Completion, payment, reports, and public documentation follow in later checkpoints.

request.description: Checks PostgreSQL connectivity. Returns 200 while available and 503 with a generic error when unavailable.
Unknown paths return a JSON error.
The health endpoint accepts GET and HEAD only.

item.name: Households
item.description: Run this folder in order. Four endpoints with positive and negative cases. It creates and removes its own household.

request.description: Required nonblank owner_name and address. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Stores the generated UUID for subsequent requests.

exec: pm.test('Fields and timestamps', function () { pm.expect(household.owner_name).to.eql('Ayu'); pm.expect(household.address).to.eql('Jl. Merdeka 1'); pm.expect(household.created_at).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(household.updated_at).to.eql(household.created_at); });

request.description: Defaults: page=1, limit=20. Sorted by created_at DESC, id DESC. Existing records are allowed.

exec: pm.test('List metadata', function () { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.data).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(body.meta.page).to.eql(1); pm.expect(body.meta.limit).to.eql(20); pm.expect(body.meta.total).to.be.at.least(1); });

request.description: Positive integer page and limit, maximum limit 100. Count and rows use the same database snapshot.

exec: pm.test('Requested page size', function () { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.data).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(body.meta.page).to.eql(1); pm.expect(body.meta.limit).to.eql(1); pm.expect(body.meta.total).to.be.at.least(1); });

request.description: Read the record created by the first request.

exec: pm.test('Stored household', function () { const household = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(household.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('household_id')); pm.expect(household.owner_name).to.eql('Ayu'); pm.expect(household.address).to.eql('Jl. Merdeka 1'); });

request.description: Broken JSON is rejected before service validation.
PostgreSQL TEXT does not accept NUL. Invalid field values are rejected before persistence.
Vertical tab is not valid JSON whitespace and must not be silently removed.
Only owner_name and address may be supplied. IDs are generated by the server.
IDs must contain hexadecimal UUID text in 8-4-4-4-12 format.
The maximum page size is 100.
JSON requests require Content-Type application/json.
JSON request bodies are limited to 64 KiB. The local variable is generated only for this request.
Deletes only the record created by this folder. A household with related pickup/payment records returns 409 household_in_use.
A valid UUID that no longer exists returns 404.
Repeated deletion returns 404 and does not affect other records.

item.name: Pickups
item.description: Run in order. Creates one dedicated household and two pickups; cancels both at the end. These records remain as history because pickups cannot be deleted. No existing data is changed. Billing policies are also exercised by isolated PostgreSQL tests until payment endpoints become available.

request.description: Creates a new household for this run. Retained with pickup history.

body.raw: {"owner_name":"Postman pickup lifecycle","address":"Dedicated local API test fixture"}

response.name: Created

request.description: Creates a pending pickup with no scheduled date.

exec: pm.test('Initial pickup', function () { const p = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(p.status).to.eql('pending'); pm.expect(p.type).to.eql('organic'); pm.expect(p.household_id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('pickup_household_id')); pm.expect(p.pickup_date).to.eql(null); pm.expect(p.safety_check).to.eql(null); });

item.name: Schedule electronic and complete safety check

request.description: Pending only. Future RFC3339 date; optional safety_check updates the stored value.

exec: pm.test('Safety and schedule persisted', function () { const p = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(p.status).to.eql('scheduled'); pm.expect(p.safety_check).to.eql(true); pm.expect(p.pickup_date).to.match(/Z$/); pm.expect(new Date(p.pickup_date).getTime()).to.eql(new Date(pm.variables.get('pickup_future_date')).getTime()); });

exec: pm.test('Both fixtures canceled', function () { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.meta.total).to.eql(2); pm.expect(b.data).to.have.lengthOf(2); b.data.forEach(function (p) { pm.expect(p.household_id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('pickup_household_id')); pm.expect(p.status).to.eql('canceled'); }); });
